problem: A particle $P$ of mass $2\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a resultant force. The particle's velocity is $2t\,m/s,$ where $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the work done by the force between the times $t=1\,s$ and $t=2\,s.$

examples.knowledge_point: Applying the Work-Energy Principle To Find the Work Done by a Force
examples.problem: A particle $P$ of mass $1\,\rm{kg}$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a resultant force. The displacement of the particle is given by $(t^2-2t+3)\,\rm{m},$ where $t \geq 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the work done by the force between the times $t=1\,\rm{s}$ and $t=3\,\rm{s}.$
examples.worked_solution:
The work-energy principle states that the work done by a resultant force on a particle equals the change in the particle's kinetic energy. That is,

$$
W
= 
\Delta\, \text{KE}
$$

where the change in kinetic energy of a particle is given by

$$
\Delta\, \text{KE} = \dfrac12 m v_1^2 - \dfrac12 m v_0^2
$$

and $m$ is the particle's mass, $v_0$ is its initial velocity, and $v_1$ is its final velocity.

The displacement of the particle is given by $x(t)=t^2-2t+3,$ where $t$ is time in seconds.
We find the velocity $v(t)$ of the particle by differentiating the displacement with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2t+3) \\  & =2t-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the particle's initial velocity, at $t=1$, is

$$
v_0 = v(1) =  2(1) -2 = 0\,\rm{m/s},
$$

and its final velocity, at $t=3$, is

$$
v_1 = v(3) = 2(3) -2= 4\,\rm{m/s}.
$$

Therefore, by the work-energy principle, the work done by the force between these times is

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =Δ\,\text{KE} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot (4)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1\cdot {0}^{2} \\  & =8-0 \\  & =8\,J.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ of mass $4\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis from rest at the origin with an acceleration of magnitude ${t}^{3}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where the acceleration acts in the direction of increasing $x,$ and $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the particle's kinetic energy at time $t=2\,s.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The kinetic energy of a particle with mass $m$ and velocity $v$ is given by

$$
\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}.
$$

When the mass and velocity are measured in kilograms and meters per second, respectively, the particle's kinetic energy is measured in Joules ($J$).

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =\int {t}^{3}\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =\frac{1}{4}{t}^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
0=\frac{1}{4}(0)^{4}+C\,⟹\,C=0.
$$

Hence, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{4}{t}^{4}.$ In particular, its velocity at time $t=2\,s$ is

$$
v=v(2)=\frac{1}{4}({2}^{4})=4\,m/s.
$$

Therefore, the kinetic energy of the particle at $t=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{KE} & =\frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot {4}^{2} \\  & =32\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
